headline: Domain-level selection and passenger mutation effects reshape cancer functional genomics
label: Cancer Genome Functional Landscapes
summary: Exome- and genome-scale tumor datasets now resolve selection at protein-domain level and functional effects of passenger mutations beyond driver genes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is linking somatic alterations to functional consequences rather than to gene-level presence alone. A domain-level selection scan of more than 9,500 TCGA exomes identifies 818 positively selected protein domains, many of which gene-based analysis misses. Analysis of more than 11,000 whole-genome tumors argues that passenger mutations in cancer genes add functional impact, supporting a continuum rather than a strict driver-passenger distinction. Melanoma patient-derived xenograft multi-omics (melPDomiX) connects mutations to transcriptomic and proteomic features to separate gain- from loss-of-function alterations. A pan-cancer single-nucleus RNA and ATAC atlas of 60 cell lines (240,957 RNA and 223,347 ATAC profiles) adds a regulatory layer, mapping gene-regulatory programs underlying intrinsic cell states.
